stance_basis: accepted Scheme A while providing conditions on playfield status and compensation for school property
summary: Board of Education District No. 170 participated in early coordination regarding the Roosevelt School property and Section 4(f) land involvement, ultimately determining that the school playfield was not significant for recreational purposes. The Board also conducted a review during preparation of the Final Statement that helped resolve the Section 4(f) question for the Roosevelt School property. Their involvement was central to resolving compensation and landscaping arrangements for the right-of-way taken from the school yard.
complaint_summary: The Board of Education District No. 170's review of the Roosevelt School Property involvement is cited as the basis for documenting alternatives to the use of Section 4(f) lands, with additional information contained in Appendix G and Chapter III.

statement.text: During the preparation of the final statement a review of the Roosevelt School Property involvement was conducted by the Board of Education, District No. 170 (See page G-7). Additional information from the review of the status of the Roosevelt School Property involvement is documented in a letter from the United States Department of the Interior, dated November 7, 1974 and contained in Appendix G, page G-5; Sheet 1 of 9 evaluation and disposition of U.S. Department of Interior Comment 1.a); and in Chapter III, page III-7.
statement.opening_anchor: During the preparation of the final statement a review of the Roosevelt School Property involvement was conducted by the Board of Education, District No. 170 (See page G-7).
statement.closing_anchor: and in Chapter III, page III-7.

summary_quote: At the regular board meeting of Wednesday, January 12, 1972, the Board of Education unamimously accepted the Building Committee's recommendation to accept Scheme A as submitted by the Department of Public Works and Buildings.
